# Sound A/B review

Each GregGuns sound compared with the Techguns sound it replaces, generated by [`tools/audio-describe`](../../../tools/audio-describe/README.md) `compare`.

> [!NOTE]
> Claude can't take audio input. Each comparison reads both sounds' spectrograms, waveforms and measurements, plus listening notes from Qwen2-Audio, which did hear both files. Scores run 0-10 for how well the replacement fills the original's role and feel.

Reviewed 278 sounds: **213 rework**, **65 tweak**, **0 keep**. Mean score 4.1.

### sounds/guns/beamgun_start_a.ogg

Replaces `sounds/guns/beamgun_start_a.ogg`. **rework**, score 2/10, confidence high.

B is a clean, rising two-tone sweep that crescendos to the very end, whereas A is a gritty, noisy sub-heavy rumble that swells fast, peaks around 0.1-0.3 s and fades out. The length and integrated loudness match, but the envelope direction, character and spectrum are essentially opposite.

| Aspect | Techguns (A) | GregGuns (B) | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| envelope/decay | Fast swell to peak by ~0.1-0.28 s (-8 dB), uneven sustain, then decay: -20 dB at 0.74 s, -40 dB at 1.0 s, ending quiet. | Starts at -17 dB, dips to -26 dB, then rises steadily to a peak at 1.24 s and cuts off abruptly at the end. It is a crescendo, not a decay. | major |
| texture/character | Gritty, choppy, crackling rumble with irregular amplitude flutter and broadband noise (flatness 0.011), like a heavy energy weapon spooling. | Smooth, pure tonal sweeps with very low flatness (0.003), clean and synthetic.
